title_zh: 宫廷古装剧：穿越千年的皇宫故事
title_en: Chinese TV Dramas (1/20): Palace Tales Across a Thousand Years
note_en: 之一 (zhīyī, "one of") comes at the end of the noun phrase, not the beginning: 最受欢迎的类型之一 is literally "most popular genres' one," i.e. "one of the most popular genres." English announces "one of" first; Chinese builds the whole group first and then adds 之一 to pick a member out of it.

sentences.en: She also said that the genre can be traced back to the serious historical dramas of the late 1990s and early 2000s, such as Yongzheng Dynasty and Kangxi Dynasty. Those productions cared more about faithfully re-creating real historical events, and their style was sober and weighty, very different from the romance-driven costume dramas that became popular later.

sentences.en: Xiao Min said that over the past decade or so, a great many costume dramas have been adapted from web novels, such as Nirvana in Fire, The Journey of Flower, and The Untamed. These works often blend political scheming, xianxia (fantasy about immortals and cultivators), and romance, which has made the genre's subject matter far richer and more varied.

sentences.en: She went on to say that the popularity of costume dramas has also fueled a revival of guofeng ("national style") culture. Many young viewers have started imitating the characters by putting on hanfu (traditional Han Chinese clothing) for photos, and some even travel to Hengdian World Studios just to experience the feeling of slipping back into ancient times, taking pictures and sharing their period looks on social media as they go.

sentences.en: Xiao Min said that today the four big video platforms, iQIYI, Tencent Video, Youku, and Mango TV, often spare no expense producing large-scale costume dramas in the fight for viewers. The industry also tends to divide the genre into two tracks: "female-oriented" works centered on palace romance and a heroine's personal growth, and "male-oriented" works that emphasize power struggles, war, and brotherly loyalty. Each attracts its own audience.

sentences.en: She added that starting in the mid-2010s, costume dramas saw a wave of "big heroine" shows (da nüzhu, dramas built around a powerful female lead), such as The Legend of Mi Yue and Princess Agents. Their heroines typically start out from humble origins, endure all kinds of hardship, and grow step by step into brilliant, powerful women capable of swaying the politics of the court, and they have won over many female viewers.

sentences.en: She also said that, beyond that, the authorities sometimes temporarily tighten broadcast approvals and prime-time slots for costume dramas to keep historical subjects from flooding the screens, which pushes the major platforms to air more realistic contemporary urban dramas for a while. Even so, with their huge fan base and considerable income from overseas rights, costume dramas have always held a position in the Chinese TV market that is hard to replace.
